inline_text:
Closes #59

## What this adds

A GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/use-cases-link-check.yml`) that checks links in `workstreams/critical-use-cases/` using [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee).

| When | What's checked | Fails? |
|---|---|---|
| PR touching the folder | All links inside the repo (files and `#anchors`), plus only the external links the PR adds or changes | Only on clearly dead links: 404/410, missing file or anchor, dead domain |
| Weekly (Mon 13:17 UTC) and manual run | Every link | Never. Updates one open issue labelled `link-health` |

The report has three sections, each naming the use case (inventory row) a link is cited in, plus the file and line:

- **Broken**: dead page, missing anchor or dead domain. Needs fixing.
- **Could not verify automatically**: 403/429, timeouts and network errors, mostly from sites that block bots. Never fails a check; a human can open these in a browser.
- **Redirected**: still works but lands on a different page (for example, anthology.com → blackboard.com), which often means a product was renamed or moved. Trivial redirects (http→https, www, trailing slash) are ignored.

Because the PR check only looks at external links the PR touches, existing rot elsewhere in the inventory won't block contributors.

### How this maps to #59's acceptance criteria

- [x] Extracts every URL from the inventory. It checks all links in the folder, a superset of the Notes column.
- [x] Records the result for each link: resolves, redirects, 404, timeout, blocked.
- [x] Failures are actionable: use case name, URL, failure type, file:line.
- [x] Redirects are flagged separately from hard failures.
- [x] Runs on demand (`workflow_dispatch`) and on a weekly schedule.
- [ ] Stretch goal (does the page still support the claim?): not in this PR. Worth a follow-up once we see how noisy the basic check is.

On rate limiting: low concurrency (8), retries with backoff and a 30s timeout. lychee doesn't read robots.txt.

### Files

- `.github/workflows/use-cases-link-check.yml`: the two jobs
- `.github/scripts/link_report.py`: turns lychee's JSON into the Markdown report (Python standard library only)
- `lychee.toml`: retries, timeouts, browser user agent, anchor checking
- `.lycheeignore`: URLs to skip (Discord, Google Docs; both need sign-in)
- `workstreams/critical-use-cases/README.md`: short "Link checks" section, including how to run it locally

### Also fixes three broken links inside the repo

The PR check would fail on these, so they're fixed here:

- `use-case-inventory.md` linked to `./classification-schema.md` in 4 places. This is the same edit as #48, so the two merge cleanly in either order.
- Contents anchor `#it-network-ops` → `#it--network-ops`
- `schema-agentic-use-cases.md` contents anchor `#how-to-use-this-file` → `#how-to-use-this-document`

The 9 dead external links currently on `main` are **not** fixed here; that's a follow-up PR.

## Testing

Run locally with lychee 0.24.2 (the version lychee-action v2.9.0 installs):

- Internal-link check on `main`: catches the 3 issues above and exits 1. On this branch: 0 broken, exit 0.
- PR-mode simulation (a changed row plus a known-dead URL): reports the 404 with its use case and line and exits 1. Bot-blocked links show as "could not verify" and exit 0.
- Full run: 324 links, **9 broken, 27 could not verify, 44 redirected**.
- `actionlint` passes.

Also tested end to end on GitHub's runners, on my fork:

- PR check on a fork PR: passed in 14s (60 internal links, 1 changed external link, 0 broken).
- Manual run of the weekly job: created a `link-health` issue with the same results as locally (9 broken, 27 could not verify, 45 redirected). A second run updated that issue instead of opening a new one.

After merge, the first scheduled run is Monday 13:17 UTC, or a maintainer can trigger it with **Actions → Use cases link check → Run workflow**.

## Permissions

`contents: read` by default. The weekly job adds `issues: write` (to create/update the report issue and its label). Scheduled runs only happen on `aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration`; manual runs work on forks too, so contributors can try the check there first. Third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs (`actions/checkout` v7.0.1, `lycheeverse/lychee-action` v2.9.0).
